disposition_reason: Tables 2 to 4 print lead, cadmium and arsenic means for raw sardine and shrimp by governorate and season; mercury was not detected.

study.design: market survey across four coastal governorates and four seasons
study.origin: Mediterranean coast, Egypt (fish markets of the four governorates)
study.market: fish markets, Alexandria, Kafr El-Sheikh, Damietta, Port Said
study.method: microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion of 0.5 g, ICP-OES
study.qa: spike recoveries 97-99%; RSD <5%; no CRM named

controls.outcome: Pb and Cd higher in winter in both species (e.g. sardine Pb Kafr El-Sheikh 0.611 winter 2019 vs 0.352 summer 2020 mg/kg); no seasonal effect on As

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Egyptian permitted limits cited: Pb 0.3, Cd 0.05, As 2 mg/kg; Hg 0.5 mg/kg

unresolved: Text states 40% of sardine and 79% of shrimp samples exceeded the Egyptian As limit of 2 mg/kg, and that some sardine As exceeded 3 ppm, yet no table mean exceeds 0.965 mg/kg and SDs are small; the exceedance statements cannot be reconciled with Tables 2-4.
Text says shrimp Pb was below detection in summer 2021 in Alexandria and Port Said, but Table 2 prints Port Said summer 2021 as 0.074 ± 0.015 mg/kg (Port Said summer 2020 is <d.l.).
Fresh sardine and shrimp, not canned: proxy for tinned-fish only.
Arsenic is total arsenic by ICP-OES; risk uses the inorganic As RfD.
